summary: Duplicate DNS A responses from corporate NAT reflection causing TLS session duplication and presigned artifact validation errors on private deploy
description:
Issue summary: Acme Health reports sporadic presigned artifact validation failures during model shard downloads on their private deployment. Failures align with short windows when control-plane requests show duplicate DNS A answers returned to serving nodes. Impact: ~3-5% of shard fetches fail with HTTP range validation errors causing inference retries and increased latency for customer traffic. This affects live production traffic in us-east and causes customer-visible 5xxs in application logs.

Observed behavior: During the reported windows, serving nodes log back-to-back connections to the same artifact host with identical client IP but different ephemeral source ports; TLS sessions appear to be established twice in quick succession for the same logical request. Downstream S3-presigned range validation occasionally rejects the second connection due to non-monotonic byte-range delivery (range hash mismatch).

Expected behavior: Normal artifact fetches should use a single TLS session and stream consistent byte ranges. DNS queries to the control-plane should return a single authoritative A record.

Environment: Private deployment (VPC peering + corporate egress), prod us-east. Customer uses an on-prem corporate edge that performs NAT reflection for internal resolver queries.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Trigger high-rate model shard downloads from a serving node behind customer's corporate egress
2) Observe DNS responses captured from node (tcpdump -n port 53) during failure window
3) Correlate duplicate A responses to artifact hostnames with presigned URL validation failures in serving-node logs
4) Reproduce by running a DNS query loop against corporate forwarder while issuing concurrent artifact GETs to produce race conditions
logs: Mar 10 09:12:01 serving-node-7 fetcher[3241]: TLS session established to presigned.artifacts.acme.net (srcport=49156)
Mar 10 09:12:01 serving-node-7 fetcher[3241]: duplicate DNS A response received: 10.10.5.8 (orig TTL=30) then 10.10.5.8 (reflected)
Mar 10 09:12:01 serving-node-7 fetcher[3241]: GET /shard?r=abc range 0-524287 502 range-validate-failed
investigation_notes: Support replicated presigned range hash mismatch locally using captured pcap and presigned URL (see attached pcap snippet).
pcap shows two DNS A answers within 30-50ms for the same query ID originating from customer's forwarder IP and from corporate edge NAT (duplicate source).

Hypothesis: Corporate edge is reflecting or replaying DNS replies (NAT reflection / asymmetric forwarding) causing the serving node resolver library to process duplicate responses and re-open TLS connections while previous TCP stream is still establishing, leading to partial-range delivery observed by S3 backend.

We observed that re-use of ephemeral ports combined with conntrack entries at the egress appliance can cause second connection to be associated with same logical session but different TCP 4-tuple, confusing presigned range validation when ranges overlap.
SRE ran a controlled test: disabling forwarder caching at customer forwarder removed the duplicate-answer window and eliminated validation errors during the test session.
comments: Maya Chen (Support) [2026-03-10]: Customer reported increased 5xxs from model inference; initial triage points to artifact fetch failures. Collected pcaps and application logs. Escalating to SRE for network analysis.

Ravi Patel (SRE) [2026-03-11]: Observed duplicate A answers in pcap. Requesting customer's network team to run tcpdump on their forwarder and confirm whether NAT reflection is enabled on the edge appliance.

Customer (Acme Health) [2026-03-11]: Confirmed edge appliance (vendor: NetEdge) has a feature called 'resolver reflection' enabled for internal recursion; will test disabling for a short maintenance window tomorrow morning.

Ravi Patel (SRE) [2026-03-12]: Temporary mitigation applied on our serving nodes: increased validation buffer on fetcher and added stricter TLS session reuse checks to avoid immediate reconnect on duplicate DNS responses. This reduced customer 5xxs in monitored window.
Customer (Acme Health) [2026-03-12]: After disabling reflection, errors dropped to baseline. We'll coordinate to keep feature off pending permanent fix.
resolution: Workaround implemented: customer disabled 'resolver reflection' on edge appliance; platform-side mitigations deployed to serving nodes (stricter session reuse logic and a small debounce on duplicate DNS answers). Root cause: corporate NAT/reflection of resolver replies causing duplicate DNS answers and rapid TLS reconnects that triggered presigned range validation failures. Next steps: (1) Customer to keep reflection disabled in production (done), (2) Engineering to land permanent serving runtime guard to ignore duplicate A answers from different source IPs within query window (PR #4892), (3) Postmortem and network guidance doc will be added to Confluence. Related PR and runbook linked above.
